title: Log abundance in characteristic zero
main_claim: Over any algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, every nef Q-Cartier K_X+B on a projective lc pair with effective rational boundary is semiample. The proof is a dimension induction (GLM_{<n} + Iitaka-over-Albanese => NV_n => GLM_n) built on two ingredients: a signed-boundary abundance criterion, proved with root stacks, Hodge modules, formal lifting and nef reduction, and smooth canonical nonvanishing, proved by contradiction through very-general jet estimates and a Frobenius determinant comparison.

issues.description: The only companion input is OpenAIIitaka Cor 6.2, used only in its zero-boundary form over the Albanese image to show q(X)=0. The paper itself notes that Hacon-Popa-Schnell Thm 1.1 covers this use, so this is not a circular dependence. It is still an external input whose stated generality goes beyond what is used.
issues.evidence: ex:irregularity uses only kappa(B,K_B)>=0 for a base of maximal Albanese dimension and kappa(F)>=0 from the induction hypothesis.

These are the tracking and Bezout estimates P^f.V<=(2/delta)^{d-f}P^d plus subadjunction, the no-pullback descent of the current, and the special-termination argument. The smooth-nonvanishing half of a famous open conjecture rests on them, so they deserve an independent deep check. No concrete failing step was found in the parts read.

coverage: I read and checked: introduction; induction (Lemma mmp:comparison, Prop boundary-restriction via Fujino-Gongyo Thm 1.5, the trivial-perturbation length estimate a<1/m, every case of Prop inductive-reduction including the full-support G_V/negativity argument and the kappa_sigma monotonicity step); signed_geometry (the Hodge-index lemma with the Qa=0, Qa^+=0 sign argument, and the root/index-cover/blowup construction); hodge (lowest piece F_0M=R^1g_*B, negative-twist Kodaira-Saito vanishing via finite pushforward and the retraction, the obstruction derivation). In the lifting proof I re-derived the binomial identity b_j-b_i=-(a+k)eta*sigma, the right-action sign (dt/(t-h)).d_t=dt/(t-h)^2, and the symbol-kernel H^{-1} argument. I sanity-checked the r=0 case: it reduces to Du Bois surjectivity H^{N-1}(O_{(k+1)S})->H^{N-1}(O_S). In signed_descent I checked the flatness/algebraization of the null family, the countable-Hilbert-strata argument, vertical descent (Zariski lemma) and the nef-reduction bound b<=v. In frobenius I checked the finite-data theorem: jet products, generic rank via the z^p basis, diagonal filtration and socle pairing, the Langer slope bound, the flag count giving 7^n H^n p^{2n}<R/4, the determinant class B/p+(p-1)K/(2p)+lambda*S, and the 80eps vs 3/4 contradiction. I also checked the witness construction (D^+-Q_lambda psef since r>qm+1). In exclusions I checked ex:irregularity, prop:general-type (uniqueness of the current on kappa=0 fibers, web quotient, Gongyo-Lehmann), the Lelong ACC lemma with the Skoda bound nu_E<=A(E)nu_x, prop:bounded-curves (the ramification-cost bound and the DCC trick forcing an exact zero gap), signed-alternative (every flip meets the floor plus special termination), and the Hanamura fixed-cover step. In jets I read the scalar jet bound, the bundle models, and the large-Seshadri case analysis, including the lc-center construction from the coefficient-ideal polytope. Only skimmed: common-tools lemmas, no-pullback, current-comparison, special termination, completion/consequences/canonical-rings/classification/analytic sections.
